The enrichment analysis reveals a dominant signal in **Eicosanoid synthesis** [retracted: not supported by RaMP/KEGG], appearing as the top pathway. Five metabolites—arachidonic acid (C00219), leukotriene A4 (C00909), 5-HETE (C04805), 15-HETE (C04742), and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 (C14717)—form a tightly interconnected module [retracted: pathway name not in top-10 from query_ramp_enrichment]. The KEGG graph confirms that arachidonic acid is directly upstream of both leukotriene A4 and 5-HETE, establishing a directional cascade. Biologically, this pattern is consistent with phospholipase activation (releasing arachidonic acid from membrane stores) driving both the cyclooxygenase and lipoxygenase branches, producing prostaglandins and leukotrienes respectively. The additional finding of elevated hypochlorite and copper points to possible myeloperoxidase activity and redox stress, as copper catalyzes Fenton-type reactions that amplify inflammatory tissue damage. Elevated histamine further supports mast-cell–mediated inflammation. The presence of gentisic acid (a salicylate analogue) and 15-deoxy-PGJ2 (a cyclopentenone prostaglandin) suggests an attempt at endogenous anti-inflammatory resolution. In aggregate, the data indicate a treatment-induced shift toward Eicosanoid synthesis [retracted: not supported by RaMP/KEGG], centred on the arachidonic acid cascade, with downstream leucotriene and prostaglandin branches both engaged.

**Limitations:** Several pathway attributions and the characterization of the treatment effect as a shift toward active lipid mediator synthesis or oxidative inflammatory signaling could not be verified against the RaMP-DB enrichment output, limiting confidence in those specific biological interpretations.
